evidence: "This state sharing is transitive"; "You are permitted to activate agreements that involve non-primary nodes"; gpt-oss uses "full = (1 << t) - 1" and subset DP; deepseek and glm build all-pairs shortest-path data
affordance_in_statement: This state sharing is transitive: if node X shares state with node Y, and node Y shares state with node Z, then node X and node Z also share identical state. You are permitted to activate agreements that involve non-primary nodes; if utilizing them as transitive conduits reduces the overall licensing cost, it is a valid strategy.
secondary_shortcut_name: Small terminal set enabling subset dynamic programming
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: transitive connectivity through optional non-primary vertices is the core minimum-Steiner-tree task. It can only be re-presented as selecting a minimum-cost connected subgraph containing all primary ledgers, which does not remove the underlying affordance.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats the problem as a weighted undirected connectivity problem and begins with all-pairs shortest-path preprocessing, suitable for Steiner-tree optimization.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement explicitly permits non-primary nodes as transitive conduits.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses subset-state dynamic programming over the at-most-10 primary ledgers.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The primary-ledger limit is at most 10, while non-primary nodes may connect terminal subsets.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest paths to exploit transitive routes through intermediate nodes.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: State sharing is transitive and agreements involving non-primary nodes are explicitly valid.

common_affordance: The requirement is connectivity of all primary ledgers, with paths allowed to share edges and pass through non-primary nodes.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its approach appears to reduce the problem to shortest paths or an MST over primary-ledger distances, which can double-count shared edges and miss the cheaper Steiner tree using a common non-primary conduit.

recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving edit can defeat all surviving solutions: their shared approach is the intrinsic graph-connectivity structure of the task. Rewording it as a minimum connected subgraph containing all primary ledgers would preserve the same problem.
